frameworks.name: North Star Metric for Franchising
frameworks.definition: Unit economics (restaurant profitability per location) is the single core lever that determines franchise sellability and growth speed.

frameworks.name: Capital Deployment Trade-off Analysis
frameworks.definition: Comparing return on equity across three paths: scaling corporate locations to 100 (franchise-heavy model), scaling to 20 corporate locations with improved margins, or franchising strategically.

claims.text: Franchises cannot be sold through active sales tactics because franchise purchase represents a lifestyle change; they can only be purchased by self-motivated buyers who must make the decision themselves.
claims.speaker: Restaurant owner (guest)

claims.text: The core franchising problem is solved by fixing unit economics: if a single restaurant location costs $100k to open and generates $500k year-one profit, franchisees sell themselves without additional sales effort.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Compelling unit economics eliminate the need for active franchise sales; the offer becomes self-liquidating.

numbers.axis: unit economics (opening cost vs year-one profit)

bounded_by: Assumes historical profitability of existing locations can be disclosed under FTC franchise disclosure requirements

claims.text: A franchisee should buy based on observable facts of existing location performance, not promises: disclose actual metrics from your open locations and tell the truth about what they have achieved.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: For a barbecue restaurant franchise with $100M system-wide revenue goal at 7% royalty, franchisee economics are: $7M annual royalty revenue, approximately $2.8M annual EBITDA at 40% net franchise margins, resulting in a ~$36M enterprise value exit (multiplied by 12x) with 30%+ founder rollover requirement, yielding $22-23M post-rollover equity value.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: franchise system at scale ($100M system-wide revenue)
bounded_by: Assumes 12x exit multiple; realistically may be 10-15x
Assumes clean 40% net margins at franchise level, which requires operational excellence

claims.text: An alternative growth path for the barbecue franchise is to scale from 4 corporate locations to 20 corporate locations (instead of pursuing 100-location system-wide growth), improve per-location profitability from $500k to $1M per location, and exit at approximately $80M (20 locations x $10M EBITDA / $1M per location profit x 8x multiple) which may exceed the 100-location franchise path's post-rollover value.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: owner-operator scaling model preferred over franchise-heavy model
claims.mechanism: Corporate ownership compounds exit value faster than franchise royalty streams when unit profitability is high and founder margin contribution is significant.

numbers.axis: exit value comparison: 100-location franchise vs 20-location corporate scaling

bounded_by: Assumes founder can efficiently operate 20 locations; Hormozi's founder-decay model (§46) suggests 20-location corporate may underperform relative to founder availability
Does not account for franchise system's brand leverage or multi-unit leverage

claims.text: Panda Express runs 27% net margins with infrastructure to support 3,000 stores and corporate overhead; a smaller regional barbecue franchise should be able to achieve comparable net margins if unit economics are optimized.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Scale and process discipline compress costs relative to revenue; Panda Express provides a systems benchmark for achievable margin structures.

numbers.axis: net margin benchmark by operator scale

bounded_by: Panda Express operates centralized commissaries and supply chain; regional operator overhead may be proportionally higher
Assumes no fundamental operational or cost-structure differences between Panda Express and barbecue franchise

claims.text: Current barbecue restaurant group ($9M top-line revenue, 4 corporate + 1 franchised location) is generating approximately $1.2M profit, which implies roughly 13% net margin; fixing restaurant unit profitability is a prerequisite to scaling franchises, because poor franchise unit economics prevent both scaling the franchise system and scaling corporate ownership.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Unit-level profitability is the bottleneck that blocks both growth paths (franchise and corporate); addressing it unblocks both.

claims.text: The path forward is a 24-month effort to optimize every dollar of unit economics to make the restaurant significantly more profitable; the outcome is fixable and the direction is clear, even though the work is non-trivial.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: willingness to commit 24 months to operational optimization
restaurant with clear profitability improvement levers

examples.text: The barbecue restaurant owner described their model: 4 corporate-owned locations generating $9M system-wide revenue, 1 franchised location (test case), and 2 additional signed franchise agreements. The goal is $100M system-wide revenue. Current per-location profit is approximately $300k (implied from $1.2M profit / 4 corporate locations). This concrete case demonstrates the tension between scaling via franchising (which requires proof of compelling unit economics) and scaling corporate-owned locations (which requires founder bandwidth and capital).

Alex Hormozi walked through a specific financial model: if the barbecue franchise scales to 20 corporate locations at $1M profit per location, they would achieve $20M EBITDA, which at an 8x exit multiple yields $160M gross value. With 30% founder rollover, the founder nets roughly $80M post-exit. This contrasts with the 100-location franchise model yielding $22-23M post-rollover, illustrating that corporate scaling can provide superior returns if profitability per location is sufficiently high.

practices.text: Disclose actual performance metrics from your existing franchise locations transparently; state the facts about what your open locations have achieved and let those results speak for themselves.

Spend 24 months optimizing restaurant unit economics down to the penny, treating every cost as a variable to improve; test new operational structures, supply chain approaches, and delivery ratios before scaling the franchise system.

Model multiple capital deployment paths (franchise to 100 locations, corporate to 20 locations, franchise + corporate hybrid) and calculate post-rollover equity value for each to determine which path aligns with founder goals and capital return expectations.
